cases.description: Repair resources with brew update-python-resources while preserving the extras marker, then rebuild and verify.
cases.prompt: The weekly update bumped my formula 'widget' to a new version but a resource now fails to build. The formula was created with the tui extra (it has a `# homebrew-tap:extras=tui` comment). How do I repair it? This is a regression-derived desk exercise: do not edit the repo, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the tap files, scripts and workflow jobs you would inspect. Answer concretely and direct the reproducing and checking rather than doing it.

rubric_items.text: Regenerates resources with brew update-python-resources rather than hand-editing resource blocks, passing --package-name widget[tui] from the homebrew-tap:extras comment.
Keeps the extras comment and the livecheck block intact.
Rebuilds from source and runs brew test, not just brew audit, and finishes with homebrew-verify and README regeneration.
Notes the weekly workflow reverts a failing formula and warns, so the log's per-formula warning, not the job status, shows the failure.

rubric_items.text: Downloads the real asset and computes the checksum from those bytes instead of copying one from an error message.
Requires an uninstall pkgutil stanza with the package identifier read from the asset, and keeps the URL version-templated.
Runs brew audit --cask --strict --online by name and hands off to homebrew-verify.

rubric_items.text: Verifies the real release asset, its checksum and the app or pkg stanzas before activating, and lets brew bump-cask-pr fill the version and checksum.
If no real asset exists, leaves the placeholder, reports activation blocked, and never fabricates a digest.
